title: Agentic Virtual Cells (AVCs): From Cell Models to Auditable Discovery Systems
content: Virtual cells, computational models that predict how cellular state changes under genetic, chemical or environmental perturbation, are increasingly built, queried and revised by artificial intelligence (AI) agents rather than by human modellers alone. Here we argue that the consequential change is not a further increase in the capacity of any single model but the explicit implementation of an operator layer: the decisions about which model to trust, which evidence to add and which experiment to run that human modellers have always made implicitly. We define an agentic virtual cell as a coupled system of a predictive cell model, an agent policy, an evidence ledger and a laboratory interface, and we distinguish four couplings through which agents and virtual cells interact: agents use models as instruments, build models, plan with models as world models and learn from models as verifiers. Drawing on the 2025 Virtual Cell Challenge, recent benchmark disputes and the first agent-built and agent-operated systems, we show that current performance limits arise jointly from model capacity, coverage of biological context and evaluation design, and that agents can relieve the second but cannot, by orchestration alone, create causal identifiability. We propose a two-tier evaluation of model outputs and agent trajectories and state five falsifiable predictions for the next five years.
